sections.content:
15,350 people

were counted on the census as "sports players" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Professional sportsmen and women train and compete, either individually or as part of a team, in their chosen sport for financial gain.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "sports players" there were more men than women (85.9% compared with 14.1%).

This means "sports players" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "culture, media and sports occupations".

Men made up 85.9% and women made up 14.1% of "sports players"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "sports players" included:

  • process operatives (other)
  • furniture makers and other craft woodworkers
  • gardeners and landscape gardeners

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally younger

The occupation of "sports players" had a younger age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 20 to 24 years. Of the whole working population 7.9% were aged 20 to 24 years. For people working as "sports players", 26.6% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "sports players" was 65 years or older.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "sports players" included:

  • coffee shop workers
  • bar staff
  • waiters and waitresses

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "sports players" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "sports players" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "sports players", 3.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a younger age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (55.8% compared with 44.2%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (72%) than self-employed (28%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
